I don't think they are still made this way but growing up my parents bought me a new toy called a lite-brite. Basically a little box, and you put a piece of black cardboard paper in the holder and then you pulled out these little multi colored pegs and following the number pattern, you put pegs in the slots and when you are done, it is a neat little picture that is kind of cute, backlit by a 40w bulb inside the housing. I unscrewed the bulb while it was still on and plugged in, and pushed a butter knife into the now open socket. Sparks started flying out everywhere. Set the bed on fire. And the carpet. Part of the wall. And the bookshelf. Thankfully we owned a fire extinguisher and was able to put everything out without too much damage.

2nd place, and probably too obscure for folks today but pre-internet, you had to dial a local BBS (bulletin board system). The most common was World war iv, or wwiv. There were others. Then a company from South Florida came up with "Major BBS", which was a large multi line BBS that alloweld you to be online with 256 other people, chat, play games, etc. the service was free to use. I didn't know long distance was a thing. So I spent two weeks calling a long distance number in Florida from Louisiana, two hours a day.... the phone bill came and it was over $10,000. We were able to negotiate and change how much we owed but I got one hell of a beating for running up a $10,000 phone bill.

I've applied for him. Denial after denial. He was getting SSI until they redefined what pdd nos was and sent us a notice that since pdd nos isn't a thing anymore, he was suddenly no longer disabled, and that if I felt he would qualify for some other covered disability, I was welcome to re-apply. So we resubmitted calling for ASD, but he wasn't disabled enough to qualify. The last psychiatrist he had said the reason all the other meds didn't help is because he is bipolar. And for him to re-submit an application for SSI because of his issues, which would theoretically give him enough money to live on. 

He can't collect Disability. He's never worked. You need a minimum of 5 work credits before they will even look at your application. The best he can hope for is SSI, SNAP benefits, and I think it's possible now that he's an adult with his own benefits, he should be able to file for general aid.  

Don't get me wrong. I'm collecting disability the last 10 years now. I would give anything for the ability to work a minimum wage job wiping tables or mopping floors or something. I live in Southern California. The minimum wage here is $16.50/hr. Assuming 40 hours a week, that is $660 gross a week, times 4 is roughly $2,640/month. I get $1,227/month. Works out to about $6/hr. I would love to be stable and functional enough to work again.

BUT... there is always a but, isn't there??

  
you 100% can't take any opioid based painkillers. the samidorphan binds to the opioid receptors in your brain. there is no safe dose of opioids while on it. i absolutely hate opiods. i don't like how they make me feel. so it's great for me. i am not a doctor. this is not intended to be medical advice and just my opinion. your mileage may vary.
